findings.highlight: The material of the glass, its composition, the flow of its power...I can see it as if it were a network of blood vessels.
findings.evidenceJa: ガラスの材質とカタチ、力の流れ、人間でいうところの血管まで図面にできる
findings.governingReading: Shirou can diagram the glass material and shape, the flow of power, and even what would be blood vessels in a human.
findings.explanation: The lamp’s shape and Shirou’s ability to turn even the vessel network into a diagram are collapsed into “composition” and a visual simile.

findings.highlight: I couldn't control myself, and I ended up using more magical energy than I should have
findings.evidenceJa: コントロールできなかったのか、適量を超えて魔力を注ぎ込んだ結果
findings.governingReading: Shirou could not control the infusion and exceeded the proper amount of magical energy.
findings.explanation: Failure to control the amount of magical energy becomes failure to control himself.

findings.highlight: I was absolutely baffled by your lack of skill
findings.evidenceJa: アンタの才能のなさに呆れた
findings.governingReading: Rin says she is appalled by Shirou’s lack of 才能, his aptitude or talent.
findings.explanation: Rin’s accusation of absent talent becomes a lack of acquired skill.

findings.highlight: I get it, but
findings.evidenceJa: 言っているコトは判らないが
findings.governingReading: He concedes nothing about her reasoning before telling her not to insult Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: Shirou says he does not understand Rin’s argument; the English says he does.

findings.highlight: a red candy drops into my hand
findings.evidenceJa: 赤っぽいドロップを出した
findings.governingReading: The tin yields a reddish drop; it is tasteless and stone-like, and Rin later identifies it as a jewel.
findings.explanation: A red, candy-like drop is identified as candy before Rin reveals that it is a jewel.

findings.highlight: My throat's tingling
findings.evidenceJa: 食道がヒリヒリする
findings.governingReading: After swallowing, Shirou says his esophagus stings.
findings.explanation: Pain in the esophagus is moved to the throat.

findings.highlight: a compulsory learning device
findings.evidenceJa: 無理矢理判らせる為の強制装置
findings.governingReading: The jewel is a 強制装置 that forcibly makes Shirou understand or experience what he has not understood.
findings.explanation: Rin’s coercive mechanism becomes a “learning device.”

findings.highlight: it starts to get weird
findings.evidenceJa: その異状はやってきた
findings.governingReading: An abnormal condition suddenly reaches or overtakes Shirou.
findings.explanation: The arrival of a bodily abnormality becomes things “getting weird.”

findings.highlight: I furrow my brow and try to concentrate, or I know I'll fall over.
findings.evidenceJa: 意識を眉間に集めて、ぎゅっと絞っていなければ立っていられない
findings.governingReading: Shirou gathers his awareness at the point between his eyebrows and holds it tightly so he can remain standing.
findings.explanation: Concentrating consciousness between the eyebrows becomes physically furrowing the brow.

findings.highlight: it should slowly ease up as long you can maintain this state
findings.evidenceJa: 今の状態を維持していれば少しずつ楽になる
findings.governingReading: Rin says the pain should ease so long as Shirou maintains the state.
findings.explanation: The fixed phrase “as long as” loses “as.”

findings.highlight: The moment we are born with it...or rather, the moment it's made, is when we're separated into electric kettles and plain, insulated bottles.
findings.evidenceJa: 生まれつき—いえ、作られる時に電気ポットか保温瓶か分けられる
findings.governingReading: People are sorted at birth—or rather, when they are made—into electric kettles and thermoses.
findings.explanation: The kettle analogy acquires a dangling “born with it” whose referent does not exist in the Japanese sentence.

findings.highlight: your father may have been misinformed too
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方の父親も、同じ勘違いをしていたのかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Rin allows that Shirou’s father may have held the same mistaken belief.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu possibly sharing Shirou’s misconception becomes Kiritsugu having been misinformed.

findings.highlight: how the hell I am supposed to do that?
findings.evidenceJa: そんなものどうしろっていうのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks how he is supposed to turn the switch off.
findings.explanation: The question has declarative word order after “how.”

findings.highlight: all you have to do is press it. It should open your Magic Circuit
findings.evidenceJa: あとはそれを切り替えるだけで、とりあえず魔術回路は簡単に開ける
findings.governingReading: Once the mental button becomes clear, Shirou can switch it and thereby open the circuit easily.
findings.explanation: A button that must be switched between states becomes a button that is merely pressed to open the circuit.

findings.highlight: opening your Magic Circuit up
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと魔術回路が開いている状態
findings.governingReading: Shirou is in the opposite state from before: his Magic Circuit is open the whole time.
findings.explanation: A circuit that remains continuously open becomes a circuit that is “opening ... up.”

findings.highlight: I find myself thinking that Tohsaka might just be a good person.
findings.evidenceJa: 照れている遠坂をいいヤツだな、とぼんやりと思ってしまった
findings.governingReading: Because of the heat, he vaguely thinks the embarrassed Rin is a good person.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s perception that Rin is embarrassed disappears from his moment of affection.

findings.highlight: I didn't manage to succeed in my magecraft a single time.
findings.evidenceJa: 一回も“強化”が成功しなかった
findings.governingReading: Despite enduring the heat, Shirou has not succeeded at Strengthening even once.
findings.explanation: Failure at Strengthening specifically becomes failure at magecraft in general.

findings.highlight: these lamps broke because it couldn't hold all your magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: こっちは士郎の魔力に耐えきれなくなって割れたもの
findings.governingReading: The lamps broke because they could not withstand Shirou’s magical energy.
findings.explanation: Plural “lamps” takes the singular pronoun “it.”

findings.highlight: It's one of the most difficult disciplines.
findings.evidenceJa: 難易度的には最高ね
findings.governingReading: Because it constructs everything from nothing with the user’s energy, its difficulty is the highest.
findings.explanation: Projection’s difficulty is reduced from the highest level to one among several difficult disciplines.

findings.highlight: then it'll be time to think about the next steps
findings.evidenceJa: あとは手順の問題だ
findings.governingReading: Once Shirou masters the switch, what remains is a procedural problem.
findings.explanation: A known remaining matter of procedure becomes a future need to think about what the next steps are.

findings.highlight: you've been cursed with poor mentors
findings.evidenceJa: 師に恵まれていないのかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Archer paradoxically suggests Shirou has not been fortunate in his teachers, then explains that Rin is too good a student to understand him.
findings.explanation: Not being blessed with suitable teachers becomes being cursed with poor mentors.

findings.highlight: You're better off with a mage who has no talent.
findings.evidenceJa: 何も判っていない魔術師の方がうまく作用する
findings.governingReading: Archer says someone ignorant of magecraft would work better on Shirou because a genius cannot understand an ordinary person’s problem.
findings.explanation: A mage who understands nothing becomes a mage with no talent.

findings.highlight: Rin is far too brilliant
findings.evidenceJa: 凛は優等生すぎるから
findings.governingReading: Archer frames Rin as an 優等生 whose correct schooling prevents her from seeing a dropout’s peculiar error.
findings.explanation: Rin being too much of a model student becomes her being too brilliant.

findings.highlight: If so...bring it on.
findings.evidenceJa: 今なら買うぞ、二束三文で
findings.governingReading: After asking whether Archer is selling him a fight, Shirou says he will buy it for next to nothing.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s cheap purchase of the fight Archer is “selling” becomes a generic challenge.

findings.highlight: You're not fit for fighting, Shirou Emiya.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮士郎は格闘には向かない
findings.governingReading: 格闘 refers to close or hand-to-hand combat before Archer redirects Shirou toward a mental battle.
findings.explanation: Archer rules out hand-to-hand combat specifically; the English rules out fighting altogether.

findings.highlight: What a joke. I can't believe I'm giving advice to someone I should be killing.
findings.evidenceJa: どうかしているな、殺すべき相手に助言をするなど
findings.governingReading: Archer says he must be out of his mind to advise someone he should kill.
findings.explanation: Archer’s judgment that he himself is behaving strangely becomes the impersonal “What a joke.”
